barriers.description: Using a mock-up instead of a fully functional prototype limited functionality and required extra interviewer support, preventing observation of natural user interactions and impairing evaluation of the values clarification exercise.
barriers.justification: This methodological/resource constraint hindered the designers' ability to evaluate designs and integrate feedback because it stopped them observing real user behavior and produced glitches that distorted usability and comprehension testing.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, asking users to review a mock-up instead of a finished product requires much more involvement from the interviewer, which prevented us from observing real user interaction with the web-based decision aid. ... However, the mock-up functionality was limited and caused some unintended glitches. ... the mock-up clearly impaired understanding of the values clarification exercise.

barriers.description: Difficulty recruiting participants due to reliance on health care providers and the vulnerability of the target population resulted in small, non-diverse samples and constrained quantitative evaluation.
barriers.justification: External stakeholder gatekeeping and population vulnerability limited the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement, manage evolving user understanding across diverse subgroups, and evaluate designs quantitatively (e.g., preventing statistical testing and broader sampling).
barriers.reference_excerpt: As we experienced challenges recruiting participants with this strategy, we also invited people with MCI who were registered in a Quebec database managed by one of us (CH). ... The vulnerability of the population made it hard to recruit subjects with the help of HCPs, as they wanted to protect them from the hassles of a research project. Consequently, we had to rely on alternative strategies to recruit older adults with MCI. We could not, therefore, diversify the participants who helped at each evaluation round, for example, for levels of MCI, educational background, and technology skills.

barriers.description: Participants often reported that they understood the content even when interviewers observed misunderstandings, making it difficult for researchers to elicit genuine difficulties through self-report alone.
barriers.justification: This interactional/emotional issue impeded managing user understanding and evaluating designs because designers could not rely on direct participant comments and had to depend on more involved observational and teach-back methods to surface true usability problems.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, having the users communicate their difficulties was not always easy because they generally felt that they understood the content even when it was clear to the interviewer that they had not.
